Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Bajaj Housing Finance Limited Q2 FY27

Ajit Kumar: 
Thank you, Neerav. Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call of Bajaj Housing Finance. I would like to thank the management of Bajaj 
Housing Finance for giving us this opportunity to host the call.

Kalani, Chief Financial Officer; and the entire senior management team. We will have opening 
comments from the management team, post which we will open the floor for Q&A.

Atul Jain: 
Thank you, Ajit and JM team for hosting us. A very good evening and welcome to the BHFL 
Q2 Earnings Call. I have the entire senior management team members with me. We have 
uploaded investor presentation on our website and stock exchanges. Hope you got a chance to 
go through the same. I'll focus on key updates from the same presentation for the quarter, which 
should take around 10 to 12 minutes, and then we'll open the forum for the Q&A.  
 
I'm on Panel Number 3 on the presentation. Last quarter witnessed two significant milestones 
for the company. We crossed landmark INR1.5 lakh crores AUM driven by strong and 
diversified growth. Along with that, Sambhav loans crossed monthly disbursement run rate of 
INR500 crores during the quarter. 
 
Overall good quarter across growth, asset quality, and profitability. Disbursements increased by 
25% on a Y-o-Y basis, and AUM growth also was 25% on a Y-o-Y basis. PAT growth was 18% 
Y-o-Y to INR980 crores in Q2, while ROA was 2.2%, and ROE improved to 12.7%. Operating 
efficiency continues to improve with opex to NTI ratio at 19.1% as against 19.7%, which was 
in Q2 last year. 
 
Asset quality remains stable with GNPA of 29 bps and NNPA of 12 bps, same in line with last 
quarter, and operational network today 223 branches across 182 locations. Capital adequacy was

21.24%, and principal business criteria stood at 60.49% as of 30th September '26 against the 
60% regulatory criteria.  
 
I'm moving to the next Panel, which are quarterly financial indicators. Total AUM stood at 
INR1.58 lakh crores as of 30th September, and a quarterly AUM addition was close to INR8,580 
crores this quarter against INR6,329 crores in Q2 of last year. Product growth across anchor 
products was good. 
 
Home loans AUM improved to 22% growth in Q2 against 20% in last quarter, while LRD growth 
was also strong at 39% against 41% growth in Q1. LAP grew 26%, and DF grew 13% on Y-o-
Y basis. AUM mix remained well-diversified with a higher home loan composition at 53.9%. 
Disbursement momentum was good during the last quarter with 25% growth, moving from 
INR15,900 crores to INR19,900 crores in Q2 FY27. 
 
I'm moving to Panel Number 5. The cost of funds reduced by 17 bps on sequential basis from 
7.2% in Q1 to close to 7% in Q2 FY27. It was mainly due to conversion of fixed-rate NCDs to 
floating-rate instrument. We always used to follow this strategy, and we had accelerated that 
strategy in Q2. 
 
Borrowing mix continue to have a higher money market mix at 56%, followed by bank lines at 
35%, and NHB at 9%. Total gross spreads improved by 7 bps driven largely by COF moderation 
of 17 bps, thereby it was able to offset 10 bps portfolio yield reduction and NIM moderated 
slightly by 2 bps sequentially to 3.7% in Q2 FY27 and opex to NTI, as already called out, 
improved 57 bps from 19.7% in Q2 FY26 to 19.1% in Q2 FY27. 
 
Moving to the next panel. Asset quality was stable during the quarter with GNPA flat on 
sequential basis at 29 bps and NNPA at 12 bps. Credit cost overall moderated by 6 bps on Y-o-
Y basis to 10 bps in Q2 FY27 against 16 bps in Q2 FY26. 
 
Thereby, PAT increased by 18% Y-o-Y to INR757 crores from INR643 crores in the same 
quarter last year. Annualized ROA, 2.2% in the current quarter, it was 2.3% in the last year Y-
o-Y in Q2 FY26, while ROE improved from 12.2% in last year to 12.7% in the current year Q2.

on the previous panels. Net NTI growth was 15%, if I have to just call out separately what has 
not been called out, on Y-o-Y basis from INR1,090 crores to INR1,254 crores, and PBT at 18%, 
INR980 crores. 
Coming to half-yearly performance, NTI grew 16% to INR2,429 crores in H1, while opex 
growth was 10% on Y-o-Y basis to INR470 crores. Both PBT and PAT growth was 20% to 
INR1,908 crores and INR1,472 crores, respectively, for first half of the year and opex to NTI 
improved from 20.4% in H1 FY26 to 19.3% in H1 FY27, and credit cost was 8 bps in H1 FY27. 
ROA for the half year also stood at 2.2%, and ROE at 12.6% in H1 FY27. 
 
I will move to Panel Number 23. As already called out, portfolio yield moderated by 10 bps 
sequentially from 8.9% in Q1 to 8.8% in Q2, while cost of funds dropped from 7.2% to 7% in
